provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Revision of senses
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list the five senses.
The pupils should be able to identify objects using each sense.

Introduction:
Last term we learned about our body parts. Today we will learn about our five senses.

Content:
We have five senses. They are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch. Sight helps us see with our eyes. Hearing helps us hear with our ears. Smell helps us smell with our nose. Taste helps us taste with our tongue. Touch helps us feel with our skin.

Class activity:
Play a game where pupils identify objects by covering each sense one by one.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name one sense.
2. What part of the body do we use for sight?
3. How does smell help us?

Summary:
Our five senses help us understand the world around us.

topics.title: The human body: bones
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state that bones hold the body.
The pupils should be able to identify major bones in the body.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about our five senses. Today we will learn about the bones in our body.

Content:
Bones are hard parts inside our body. Bones hold our body up. Without bones we would be like a bag of water. The skull protects our brain. The backbone helps us stand straight. Our legs have bones that help us walk.

Class activity:
Draw a simple body map and let pupils mark where they think the bones are.

Evaluation questions:
1. What do bones do in our body?
2. Name one bone in our body.
3. Why do we need bones?

Summary:
Bones are important for holding our body and helping us move.

topics.title: Muscles and movement
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain that muscles help us move.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate different movements.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about bones. Today we will learn about muscles that help us move.

Content:
Muscles are soft parts of our body. Muscles help us move our arms and legs. When muscles pull on bones, we can move. We use muscles to walk, run, jump and even eat. Muscles get stronger when we use them often.

Class activity:
Pupils will bend and stretch different parts of their body to feel their muscles working.

Evaluation questions:
1. What do muscles help us do?
2. Name one way we use muscles.
3. What happens when we use muscles often?

Summary:
Muscles are important for all the movements we make every day.

topics.title: Food groups
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list energy and body building foods.
The pupils should be able to sort foods into groups.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about muscles. Today we will learn about different kinds of food.

Content:
Food gives us energy and helps our body grow. Energy foods like rice and yam give us strength to play. Body building foods like beans and meat help us grow big and strong. We need both kinds of food to be healthy.

Class activity:
Pupils will sort picture cards of foods into energy foods and body building foods.

Evaluation questions:
1. What do energy foods do for us?
2. Name one body building food.
3. Why do we need different kinds of food?

Summary:
We need energy foods and body building foods to stay healthy and grow.

topics.title: Why we eat
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why we eat food.
The pupils should be able to list good eating habits.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about food groups. Today we will learn why we eat food.

Content:
We eat food to get energy to play and learn. Food helps us grow big and strong. Good eating habits help us stay healthy. We should eat at regular times. We should wash our hands before eating. We should eat fruits every day.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw a picture of themselves eating healthy food.

Evaluation questions:
1. Why do we eat food?
2. What is one good eating habit?
3. What happens if we don't eat well?

Summary:
We eat food to get energy and grow, and good habits help us stay healthy.

topics.title: Common plants
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify trees, grasses and flowers.
The pupils should be able to name common plants in their environment.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about why we eat. Today we will learn about common plants around us.

Content:
Plants are living things. Trees are tall plants with woody stems. Grasses are small green plants that grow in fields. Flowers are plants with colorful petals. We see plants in our school, homes and markets. Some plants give us food like mango and banana.

Class activity:
Go for a leaf walk around the school to collect and identify different types of leaves.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name one type of plant.
2. Where can we find plants?
3. What do some plants give us?

Summary:
There are different types of plants all around us that we can see every day.

topics.title: Parts of a plant
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify the parts of a plant.
The pupils should be able to label the parts of a plant.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about common plants. Today we will learn about the parts of a plant.

Content:
Plants have different parts. The root grows under the soil and takes in water. The stem holds the plant up and carries water. The leaf makes food for the plant using sunlight. The flower makes seeds for new plants. Some plants have fruits that contain seeds.

Class activity:
Pupils will label the parts of a plant on a diagram provided by the teacher.

Evaluation questions:
1. What does the root of a plant do?
2. Name two parts of a plant.
3. What does the leaf do for the plant?

Summary:
Plants have roots, stems, leaves and flowers that help them grow and make food.

topics.title: Common animals
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify farm and home animals.
The pupils should be able to group animals correctly.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about plants. Today we will learn about common animals around us.

Content:
Animals are living things. Farm animals are animals we keep on farms like cows and chickens. Home animals are animals we keep in our homes like dogs and cats. Some animals live in the wild like monkeys and birds. Animals need food, water and shelter to live.

Class activity:
Pupils will group picture cards of animals into farm animals and home animals.

Evaluation questions:
1. Name one farm animal.
2. Where do home animals live?
3. What do all animals need to live?

Summary:
There are different types of animals that live in farms, homes and in the wild.

topics.title: Animal body parts
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify animal body parts.
The pupils should be able to match body parts to animals.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about common animals. Today we will learn about animal body parts.

Content:
Animals have different body parts. Wings help birds fly. Legs help animals walk and run. Tails help animals balance and communicate. Some animals have fur to keep them warm. Others have scales to protect their bodies.

Class activity:
Pupils will match pictures of animal body parts to the correct animals.

Evaluation questions:
1. What do wings help animals do?
2. Name one animal body part.
3. How do tails help animals?

Summary:
Different animals have different body parts that help them survive and move.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall what they learned this term.
The pupils should be able to answer questions about the topics covered.

Introduction:
This week we will revise all we learned this term and have a fun quiz.

Content:
We learned about our five senses, bones, muscles, food groups, why we eat, plants, animals and their body parts. All these things help us understand our bodies and the world around us. Being healthy means taking care of our body and eating good food.

Class activity:
Play a class quiz game with questions about all the topics covered this term.

Evaluation questions:
1. What are the five senses?
2. What do muscles help us do?
3. Name one plant part.
4. Why do we eat food?

Summary:
We have learned many important things about our bodies and living things this term.
